case_title: Asim Shariff v. National Investigation Agency
accused_victim_relationship: No prior enmity; prosecution admitted there was no animosity between the accused and the victim. No other relationship described.
evidence_type: Circumstantial and documentary evidence (call data records, bank account details, seized banner, disclosure report, purse letter); recovery evidence. Prosecution's evidence as described by the parties, not tested by the Court.
confession: Alleged confession by accused no. 4 (prosecution submission only); not evaluated or relied on by the Court.
trial_court_outcome: Discharge application under s.227 CrPC dismissed; charges framed against the accused. No verdict; trial not concluded.
high_court_outcome: Writ petition under Arts. 226/227 and s.482 CrPC dismissed; trial court's order affirmed.
neutral_facts: On 16 October 2016, around midday, the victim was with several friends near a medical store when a pillion rider on a motorcycle attacked him with a sharp-edged machete, striking the right side of his neck, and then fled. The victim was declared dead on arrival at hospital. According to the prosecution, the victim was dressed in uniform during a march organised by an association that day, and his throat was cut in a single blow. The case was first registered as a murder by local police, and four persons were arrested within weeks. A fifth person, the accused, was arrested later. The investigation was then taken over by a national investigating agency, which alleged that the accused and four co-accused conspired to kill members of that association. The prosecution relied on call data records showing frequent telephone contact between the accused and co-accused before and after the incident, bank account details, and a seized banner bearing the photographs of all the accused. It also relied on a disclosure leading to a letter listing earlier killings, and on an allegation that the accused had organised indoctrination classes about eight to nine months earlier that the co-accused attended. One co-accused was alleged to have named the accused as the mastermind. The accused denied any personal animosity toward the victim and said nothing incriminating had been recovered from him.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a throat wound caused by a single blow with a machete (as alleged by the prosecution).
premeditation_planning: Prima facie conspiracy found for charge-framing only. The Court did not finally determine premeditation; this is for trial.
motive: alleged: conspiracy to kill members of a particular association (RSS) and create fear among the public
key_evidence_accepted: Charge-sheet material showing the accused's position in the organisation and frequent telephone/mobile contact with co-accused before and after the incident. Accepted only as prima facie material.
witness_credibility: Not assessed; the Court left the truth and veracity of the evidence to trial.
custody_duration: Arrested 2 November 2016; total period in custody not stated.
trial_duration: offence: 16 October 2016; trial judgment: 2 January 2018 (order on discharge application; para 21 gives 12 January 2018); High Court: 22 November 2018; Supreme Court: 1 July 2019
legal_representation: Accused: Kamini Jaiswal, Abdul Rahiman, Shereef K.A., Rani Mishra, Jatinderpal Singh (Advocates). State/NIA: Aman Lekhi, ASG, with Shraddha Deshmukh, Kanu Agrawal, B. V. Balaram Das (Advocates).
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation transferred to NIA; charge sheet filed against five accused; charges framed by the trial court.
appeal_history: Trial court: discharge dismissed and charges framed. High Court: writ petition dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Section 15 UAP Act covers individual acts and terrorist gangs, and s.20 does not require the organisation to be scheduled. The victim was attacked in uniform during a procession, with no animosity. Evidence included PFI membership, a seized banner, phone contacts, a disclosure report, indoctrination classes, and an alleged confession by a co-accused.
defence_argument: Charges based on suspicion; no incriminating material recovered; the prosecution failed to adduce evidence against the accused; the Navaratri date allegation was false; no co-accused was a member of a banned organisation, so the UAP Act charge was not sustainable.
legal_principle_applied: Under s.227 CrPC the judge may sift and weigh evidence only to decide whether a prima facie case or grave suspicion exists. If two views are possible and one shows only suspicion, discharge is warranted. No mini-trial.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal (1979) 3 SCC 4; Sajjan Kumar v. CBI (2010) 9 SCC 368; State v. S. Selvi (2018) 13 SCC 455; Vikram Johar v. State of UP (2019) 6 SCALE 794
other_sentence_order: Observations made only for disposing of the appeal and do not prejudice the trial; trial to proceed independently. Appeal dismissed.
